title: Etale local integral split models for reductive group schemes
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring and $G$ a reductive $A$-group scheme. A reductive group scheme over a commutative ring is a smooth affine finitely presented group scheme with connected geometric fibres having no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup; unipotent means that in a faithful matrix representation each geometric point $u$ satisfies $(u-I)^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$. Group objects use the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over the specified spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with smooth, affine, finite presentation and connected as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A split maximal torus is a subgroup scheme isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ with fibrewise maximal tori, where $\mathbf G_m(B)=B^\times$ and $r\geq0$. A Borel subgroup scheme has geometric fibres maximal smooth connected solvable subgroups; solvable means that iterated commutator subgroups eventually become trivial. There exist a finite nonempty set $I$, etale maps $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] with nonzero $B_i$ and jointly surjective images, split reductive $\mathbf Z$-group schemes $H_i$, and isomorphisms of $B_i$-group schemes
$$G\times_A B_i\simeq H_i\times_{\mathbf Z}B_i\quad(i\in I).$$
Here each $H_i$ comes with a split maximal torus and a Borel subgroup scheme containing it. The rings $A,B_i$ need not be Noetherian, and the groups $H_i$ may differ for different $i$. Split integral models use the split-realization convention of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]; the requested isomorphisms need not preserve any chosen pinning.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.3, printed pp.136-137; Theorems 6.1.16(2) and 6.1.17, pp.196-197 (Existence and Isomorphism Theorems), applied after trivializing root line bundles. Finite affine refinement uses quasi-compactness of Spec A. These are Conrad sources, not an SGA citation; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-etale-pinned-splitting] to $G/A$. Obtain a jointly surjective etale affine family $\operatorname{Spec}C_j\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, and on each member a pinned split realization of a based datum $\mathcal R_j$. Keep the full datum, including central lattice directions and the constant coroots; a split torus alone would not supply these.

For each $j$, apply the existence clause of [lem-sfb-pinned-split-root-classification] with base ring $\mathbf Z$ and datum $\mathcal R_j$. It supplies a pinned split reductive group $H_j/\mathbf Z$ with its specified split maximal torus. Apply [lem-sfb-split-positive-root-borel] over $\mathbf Z$ to give $H_j$ a Borel subgroup containing that torus. This constructs the models over the integers before making any isomorphism over $C_j$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-affine-refinement] to the affine base $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the cover of step 1. It gives finitely many affine opens $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ in selected $\operatorname{Spec}C_{j(i)}$, with etale jointly surjective composites to $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Drop the empty members and retain the index map $i\mapsto j(i)$. The maximal-ideal existence assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] shows that $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is nonempty: a maximal ideal is prime since, if $xy\in\mathfrak m$ and $x\notin\mathfrak m$, writing $1=a+rx$ with $a\in\mathfrak m$ gives $y=ay+rxy\in\mathfrak m$. Consequently at least one $V_i$ remains. Each remaining $B_i$ is nonzero, since a prime ideal of its nonempty spectrum is proper. Set $H_i=H_{j(i)}$, retaining its integral torus and Borel.

source.place: Finite affine refinement after the local splitting; the existing refinement leaf packages quasi-compactness and openness of etale maps

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-pinned-split-root-base-change] for $C_{j(i)}\to B_i$ to restrict the realization on $G_{C_{j(i)}}$, and for $\mathbf Z\to B_i$ to pull back the realization on $H_i$. Both resulting pinned split $B_i$-groups realize the same based datum $\mathcal R_{j(i)}$. The isomorphism clause of [lem-sfb-pinned-split-root-classification], applied to the identity of that datum, gives an isomorphism $G\times_A B_i\simeq H_i\times_{\mathbf Z}B_i$. Here the iterated fibre product is identified with $G\times_A B_i$ by the universal property of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Forget the pinnings. The finite nonempty family and the integral tori and Borels from steps 2-3 give every clause asserted. No step requires a Noetherian base or one common root datum on the whole base.

source.place: Theorem 6.1.17, p.197, applied after base change of the split data

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q56-c84cb2e93 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 5 new nodes in full against Conrad, Reductive group schemes (author PDF fetched and run through pdftotext). Checked: Def 1.3.3 p.27, Def 5.1.1, Ex 5.1.2, Lemma 5.1.3 pp.136-137, Prop 5.1.6 and g=t+sum g_a p.138, Thm 5.1.13 pp.143-144, Cor 5.2.7(2), Def 6.1.1 and Rem 6.1.2 p.186, Thms 6.1.16(2)/6.1.17 (non-empty S, equivalence on isomorphisms) pp.196-197. The def matches 5.1.1/6.1.1, including constant coroots and a constant lattice isomorphism, so the disconnected-base case of Ex 5.1.2/Rem 6.1.2 is handled. Small cases hold: empty Phi gives a torus or the trivial group, and G=T=B in the Borel node. Step 1 uses the splitting statement exactly. Step 2 uses classification existence over Z (nonzero) plus the Borel node; D_Z(M) is G_m^r. Step 3 uses the refinement leaf (affine base only, Stacks 0218) and the maximal-ideal leaf; dropping empty members leaves m>=1 and every B_i nonzero. Step 4 applies base change along C_j->B_i (affine open) and Z->B_i, then the classification isomorphism clause for u=id and the fibre-product identification. The item's only change is the convention sentence plus a stmt_dep; it pins the meaning of 'split' to Conrad 5.1.1, and its one citer, symmetric-power-dvr-reduction, is unaffected. Duplicates: lem-sfb-integral-split-root-datum and lem-sfb-integral-root-datum-isogenies (both over Z, no pinned isomorphism theorem) overlap only the Z existence part of classification. The new node is a strict generalization that step 4 needs over non-Noetherian B_i. The Borel nodes already in the DAG are for Noetherian local rings, so they do not apply over Z. The report missed the two Z nodes; this is noted in review.md, not counted as a fault. Batch 5: def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization -> lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure reaches lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change, which is the Stacks 021O Mathlib leaf for base change of fppf coverings. That is a generic fact and not part of the trace formula or Poincare duality proofs, so it is genuinely outside the assumptions. No SGA citations, no fixes.
